_comment: Antelope Zen Go Synergy Core -- reverse-engineered from USBPcap captures (Windows, VM) in sidejob/zen_go_synergy_core-filtered/ (2026-08-31), cross-checked against the zen-go-tui protocol audit and fixtures. SAME HID vendor protocol family as Orion Studio III (profiles/orion_studio_sc.json) and Discrete 8 Pro: magic 0x70 command, opcode @4, param_id @16, 320-byte reports on the same endpoints. Param IDs are largely shared with Orion; report magics and some frame shapes DIFFER (meter is 0x83 not 0x75; the mixer frame is opcode 0x16 / subcmd 0x04 with no send byte). Everything here is from observed traffic on hardware the capture owner controls. Fields carry status + evidence; anything marked 'observed' is not yet decoded. The official Antelope schema is intentionally not overlaid where it conflicts with this capture-derived Zen Go dialect.

device.name: Antelope Zen Go Synergy Core
device.notes: USB-C bus-powered 4-in / 8-out desktop interface, 2 mic/line/Hi-Z preamps, Synergy Core DSP. Composite device: UAC2 audio (interfaces 0/1/2, 16 in / 16 out, 24-bit, iso endpoints 0x05 OUT / 0x84 IN) plus a vendor HID control interface (interface 3). Device descriptor: class 0xef/0x02/0x01, bcdUSB 0x0200, iManufacturer/iProduct/iSerial 1/2/3. Config descriptor: 4 interfaces, bus-powered (bmAttributes 0x80), maxpower 500 mA.
device.evidence: capture_01_enumeration.pcapng: device descriptor frame -> idVendor 0x23e5, idProduct 0xa015, bcdDevice 0x0606; config descriptor (243 bytes) decoded. The connect-time 0x75 frame carrying ASCII 'Zen Go Synergy Core' + serial + fw rev is a readback RESPONSE for category 0x01 -- see frame.readback, not a Zen-Go-specific name report.

transport.notes: Identical transport to Orion Studio III / Discrete 8 Pro: HID interface 3, interrupt EP 0x01 OUT / 0x82 IN, 320-byte reports, bInterval 6. The HID report descriptor was not captured (the GET_DESCRIPTOR(0x22) request is outside the trace window); the Discrete 8 Pro's is 54 bytes with one 320B Input + one 320B Output report and NO Feature report -- assume the same here until dumped from Linux hidraw (tools/hid_probe.py). If it has no Report ID, Linux hidraw writes need a leading 0x00 (321 bytes) -- see family_notes.
transport.evidence: capture_01_enumeration.pcapng config descriptor: interface 3 = HID, HID desc bcdHID 0x0111 / report desc type 0x22 len 54, EP 0x82 IN + EP 0x01 OUT both interrupt maxpacket 0x0140 (320) bInterval 6.

frame._comment: Outgoing command frames: magic 0x70 @0 (cosmetic in this family), opcode @4, param_id @16. Layout after @16 depends on the opcode.

command.notes: The per-channel / per-bus setter, same as Orion's SET_PARAM. param @16, target (channel or bus id) @17, value @18. Used for: gain (0x50), input_mode (0x4f), phantom (0x51), phase_invert (0x52), bus_level (0x47), bus_mute (0x48), bus_dim (0x66), bus_mono (0x69), param 0x49 (see params), reverb_return (0x68).
command.evidence: preamps/capture_preamp_a1_gain_mic.pcapng etc: op 0x13, param 0x50, [17]=0 (preamp A1) / 1 (A2), [18] swept the gain; mode/phantom/phase in the same layout.

global_command.notes: Device-global setter, value at @17 (no channel byte). Used for sample_rate (param 0x03), clock_source (param 0x04), oscillator (0x0a), screen_brightness (0x0e) and pan_law (0x24).
global_command.evidence: capture_05_sample_rate...: op 0x12 param 0x03 value 0-6 @17. capture_06_clock_source...: op 0x12 param 0x04 value 0-2 @17.

link_command.status: capture-confirmed for preamp space 0, mixer space 3 and rack space 4
link_command.notes: Same shape as Orion: 0xa2 @16, space @17, pair_index @18, enabled @19. Space 3 (mixer) uses a logical pair index within each 16-channel mix, but reserves 16 wire selectors per mix: Mix 1 pair 0 is wire pair 0 and Mix 2 pair 0 is wire pair 16. The isolated mixer-link captures show Mix 1 selectors 0-7 and Mix 2 selectors 16-23. The durable a2 03 write is the link state setter; a2 04 companion writes were seen only for the first two pairs (wire banks 0 and 1): they are the effect-rack link of strips 1+2 / 3+4, sent before a2 03 when the L button of strip 1 or 3 is clicked (2026-11-21: a2 04 01 01 then a2 03 01 01; readback cat 0x0b index 4 body[pair]). Space 0 (physical preamp link) captured 2026-11-21: a2 00 00 01 / a2 00 00 00, readback cat 0x0b index 0 body[0]; see channels.link_pairs for its gain side effect.
link_command.evidence: capture_dsp / mixer_links/*: op 0x14 param 0xa2 [17]=3, [18] cycling pair indices, [19]=1. mixer_links/mix1_ch1_ch2_linked.pcapng also flips state_report offset 127.

mix_command.channel_base_notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-21: the strip byte is the strip NUMBER 1-16, not a 0-based index. Panel run: strip 16 = d4 04 00 10 .. / d4 04 01 10 .., strip 9 = d4 04 01 09 .., and the cat 0x04 record holds strip N at body[2*N]. Before this the profile sent the 0-based index, i.e. the strip to the left of the one shown. channel_base 1 adds one to this project's 0-based index (same as the Discrete 4).
mix_command.notes: The virtual mixer. NOTE this is opcode 0x16 (Orion's mixer is 0x17) and the sub-cmd byte @17 is 0x04 (Orion 0x05); there is NO per-strip send byte (the reverb send is its own frame, reverb_send_command). The Zen Go mixer strip is fader + pan + mute + solo: [18]=mix number (0 = Mix 1, 1 = Mix 2), [19]=strip number 1-16 (see channel_base_notes), [20]=fader raw = dB attenuation 0 (unity) .. 90 (-90 dB), [21]=pan (low 6 bits, 0x20 = centre, ~0x02 = full L, ~0x3e = full R) + mute bit 0x40 + solo bit 0x80. Whole strip state every frame. No 0x73 STATE-REPORT readback -- fader/pan/mute/solo writes produce no state_report change. The in-band 0x74/0x75 cat-0x04 layout for mix indices 0 and 1 is capture-confirmed and decoded by the profile-driven parser; live round-trip still needs hardware verification.
mix_command.evidence: mixer/capture_mixer_09_fader_unlinked...: d4 04 00 01 <fader> 20 sweeping fader. capture_mixer_07_pan...: [21] swept around 0x20. capture_mixer_11_mute: [21] = 0x60 (0x20|0x40) vs 0x20. capture_mixer_13_solo: [21] = 0xa0 (0x20|0x80). capture_08_mixer_volume_faders_on_2_mixes: [18] = 0 and 1, [19] up to 10.

output_command.status: explained 2026-11-21 -- an ordinary mix_command frame (mix 1 = HEADPHONES 2 page, strip 3, pan hard left), not an output control
output_command.notes: SUPERSEDED: the vendor panel has no output strip in the mixer; Monitor / HP1 / HP2 level, mute and dim are only the bus params 0x47 / 0x48 / 0x66 (panel run 2026-11-21). Kept for the capture reference. Old text: The big monitor knob / output volume + mute also go through opcode 0x16 / 0xd4, as d4 04 01 03 <level> <flags> -- i.e. mix index 1, channel 3, with a pan/flags base of 0x02 (not 0x20). [20] = level (0-~0x5a), [21] bit 0x40 = mute. Whether ([18]=1,[19]=3) is a real (mix,channel) address or a special output-strip selector is not pinned down. Buses 0/1/2 have their OWN setter (bus_level 0x47 / bus_mute 0x48 / param 0x66, opcode 0x13) -- see params and 'buses'. Which of these two the Launcher uses for which physical output is not fully mapped.
output_command.evidence: capture_02_volume_down / _03_volume_up: d4 04 01 03 <level> 02 sweeping level. capture_04_mute_toggle: [21] = 0x42 vs 0x02.

reverb_send_command.notes: Per-strip Gazelle Reverb (AuraVerb) send: e9 04 00 <strip 1-16> <send> <pan>. Send is attenuation, 0x00 = 0 dB .. 0x60 = off; the send pan (0x02 .. 0x20 centre .. 0x3e) is separate from the strip pan. Both bytes travel in every frame. Byte 18 was 00 on both mixer pages (the reverb belongs to mix 0); no other value is built. Same opcode as mix_command, told apart by the param byte. Readback: cat 0x18 index 0, send at body[2*strip], pan at body[2*strip+1]; the same pairs are repeated in cat 0x04 index 0 from body[69] (frame.readback.layouts mixer_state send_offset), which is what the WebUI reads.
reverb_send_command.evidence: owner's unit fw 05.04, vendor panel 1.1.26 under Wine, usbmon, panel run 2026-11-21 (zen_panel/live.log): strips 15 and 16 only; send wheeled 0x60..0x00 and back, pan 0x02..0x3e, double click = 0x20; marker pass read strip 15 send 0x2a and strip 16 send 0x21 pan 0x19 in both cat 0x18 and cat 0x04

auraverb_command.notes: Gazelle Reverb (hardware name AuraVerb). Same frame as the Orion: da 0b 00 <room> <color> <predelay> 64 <early> <late> <rich> <time> <level> <on>; every control sends the whole frame. Raw values: room, color, early, richness, time 0..100; predelay and late reflection delay 0..150; level 1..100 (the panel knob does not reach 0); byte 22 was always 0x64 and no control moves it. Byte 18 was always 00. Readback cat 0x0a index 0: one header byte, then 11-byte blocks in frame order (block 0 = this reverb: body[1..9] values, body[10] on/off, body[11] ff); three more blocks follow that nothing in the panel writes. A factory preset is one such frame; the preset name is not stored on the device.
auraverb_command.evidence: owner's unit fw 05.04, vendor panel 1.1.26 under Wine, usbmon, panel run 2026-11-21 (zen_panel/live.log): each knob swept alone over its whole range (3177 frames), FX off/on = byte 28 00/01, two presets; start and end records equal (00 51 64 00 64 0b 0d 18 42 32 01 ff ...)

output_trim_command.notes: Monitor Out Trim: cb 42 00 01 <n>, n 0..6. Byte 17 (0x42) is the payload length (opcode 0x54 = 0x42 + 0x12, the family frame rule), so this is a 66-byte payload of which only `00 01 <n>` was ever non-zero; those bytes are sent as captured, their meaning is not decoded and only this one target was seen. See params.output_trim.
output_trim_command.evidence: owner's unit fw 05.04, vendor panel 1.1.26 under Wine, usbmon, panel run 2026-11-21 (zen_panel/live.log): the seven menu entries picked in turn, cb 42 00 01 01 .. 06 then 00

routing_command.status: frame + index mapping + source banks DECODED (2026-08-31); destination groups 3, 4, 5 and banks 0x03-0x05 identified 2026-11-21
routing_command.notes: Same shape as Orion: [16]=0xd3, [17]=0x41 (=65), [18]=destination group, then an array of (source_bank, source_index) pairs from @19, stride 2, one slot per output channel of the group. Whole group re-sent on any change; no 0x73 STATE-REPORT readback. The Zen Go also answers the in-band 0x74/0x75 readback for the capture-confirmed routing indices 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9; those explicit layouts are the safe bounds used by the WebUI. The 'channel assignments' tab assigns what each MIXER INPUT STRIP listens to. THE SLOT INDEX = MIXER STRIP NUMBER - 1 (slot 0 = strip 1 ... slot 15 = strip 16), confirmed by the index_map_5_8 / 9_12 / 13_16 captures which set slot 4..15 to the oscillator one at a time. Set a slot to (0x08, 0) to mute that strip's input; there is no 'no source'.

destination_groups.0, 1, 2: 2 slots each, read only (vendor session file: HP1, HP2, MONITOR). The panel has no selector for them; they read 04 00 04 01 / 05 00 05 01 / 04 00 04 01 (the two mixes). Not addressable here.
destination_groups.3: 8 slots -- COMPUTER REC: what the computer records on Record 1-8 (DAW I/O page). It is its own group, not a mirror: the device keeps whatever is written. What looked like mirroring is the vendor panel, which treats Record n and mixer strip n as one selector and, when an ordinary source is chosen, rewrites group 3 and then 6-9 from its own model; a LOOPBACK source is written to group 3 only. This project writes group 3 alone.
destination_groups.4: 2 slots -- SPDIF OUT 1 / 2 (DIGITAL OUTS page): d3 41 04 <bank1> <idx1> <bank2> <idx2>.
destination_groups.5: 4 slots -- AFX IN: the inputs of the four effect racks (mixer strips 1-4). The source box of strips 1-4 writes only this group; in groups 3 and 6-9 the panel always sends 00 00, 00 01, 03 02, 03 03 for those four slots.
destination_groups.6, 7, 8, 9: MIX CH1..CH4 in the vendor session file: the input maps of four mixers, of which the panel shows two. 32 slots each -- slots 0-15 = the 16 mixer strips, slots 16-31 always MUTE (0x08, unused/reserved). The Launcher ALWAYS writes all four identically and in lockstep (the 'surface_propagation' captures confirm a change to one propagates to all four), so they are one logical map -- the mixer's global strip-input assignment. Per-mix level/pan/mute IS independent (capture_mixer_19); only the input assignment is shared.

source_banks.0x01: computer playback -- idx N = playback channel N+1 (confirmed: 'ch3_cp1' -> (0x01,0), 'ch4_cp2' -> (0x01,1), 'ch5_cp3' -> (0x01,2); default maps use idx up to 7)
source_banks.0x02: S/PDIF in -- idx 0/1 = L/R (from 'ch1-4 - was spdif1,spdif2...': slot 2 was (0x02,1) = spdif R)
source_banks.0x03: AFX OUT -- idx 0-3 = the outputs of effect racks 1-4. Identified by its place in the vendor session file's source list (PREAMP, COMPUTER PLAY, SPDIF IN, AFX OUT (4), LOOPBACK HP 1/MON, LOOPBACK HP 2, ...) and by use; the panel menus do not offer it, it only appears in the maps the panel writes by itself (03 02, 03 03 on strips 3-4) and on the owner's Record 1/2 (03 00, 03 01).
source_banks.0x04: LOOPBACK HP 1/MON -- idx 0/1 = the Monitor/HP1 mix. Offered only for Record and SPDIF OUT (2026-11-21: Record 8 -> 04 01).
source_banks.0x05: LOOPBACK HP 2 -- idx 0/1 = the HP2 mix. Offered only for Record and SPDIF OUT (2026-11-21: Record 8 -> 05 00, Record 4 -> 05 01).
source_banks.0x08: MUTE (pseudo-source, idx 0) -- confirmed by all the '..._mute' captures
source_banks.0x09: oscillator -- idx 0/1 = Osc 1 / Osc 2 (the test-tone source used throughout the index-map captures)
source_banks.0x0a: emumic / mic-modeled preamp -- idx 0/1 (from 'changed ch1 to emu1' -> (0x0a,0))

routing_command.destination_sources_notes: The source kinds a new assignment may use per group (mute always). From the vendor panel's menus: the two loopbacks are offered only for Record and SPDIF OUT; a mix fed back into a rack input or a mixer strip would be a feedback loop. AFX OUT is in no menu; it is allowed for Record only, where the owner's unit held it and took it back from a script write (2026-11-21). Sources already present in a group are re-sent unchanged.
routing_command.evidence: channel_assignments/*.pcapng and mixer/capture_mixer_03/04/18-30. Each single-strip capture (chN_<src>_oscillator1_<src>) changes exactly one slot and names the source; the index_map captures walk slots 4-15 through the oscillator; capture_mixer_03/04 cycle strip 11 through preamp / playback / emumic / spdif / osc / mute. output_trim_block.notes: Monitor Out Trim index n (0..6) reads as n*4 at offset 25. The same index is repeated in bits 3-5 of the Monitor status byte (offset 29), which is why that byte must be read with masks. Offset 20 = the oscillator byte, 26 = brightness (params.oscillator / params.screen_brightness).
output_trim_block.evidence: owner's unit fw 05.04, vendor panel 1.1.26 under Wine, usbmon, panel run 2026-11-21 (zen_panel/live.log): trim 1..6 then 0 gave 25:00>04>08>0c>10>14>18>00 and 29:01>09>11>19>21>29>31>01 (Monitor muted throughout)

bus_block.flags_combine_notes: The status byte is a bit field and 03 (mute + dim) does occur, but a dim WRITE does not keep the mute: dim on gives 02 and dim off gives 00, from 01 and from 03 alike (seen on Monitor and HP1; HP2 mute/dim were not clicked in that run). Only a mute write after the dim write gives 03. So this stays false and dim is refused on a muted bus (constraints.protected_mute_buses).
bus_block.notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-21: the status byte is a bit field, not the exclusive enum this profile used to declare: bit0 = mute, bit1 = dim, 03 = both. Mute on/off changes only bit0. On Monitor (offset 29) bits 3-5 also carry the Monitor Out Trim index, so an exact compare with 1 or 2 misread a muted Monitor as soon as the trim was not 20 dBu. Mono has no confirmed state-report value yet.

state_report.status: confirmed for gain / mode / phantom / phase / sample_rate / clock / bus; other offsets unmapped
state_report.notes: Continuous state report, ~4 ms. Header: [4-5] = 0x0140 (report size). Confirmed readback fields: [18] = sample-rate index (0-6, tracks the SET value ~immediately); [19] = clock-source index (0-2); [40] + channel = active-mode preamp gain (2 channels, A1 @40, A2 @41), same 'raw = dB-ish' scale as Orion, mode-dependent range (mic 0-65, line small, Hi-Z ~0-45); [42] + channel = preamp status byte (input_mode bits 0-1, phantom bit 0x10, phase bit 0x40); [28] + 2*bus = bus block (byte 0 = level 0-96, byte 1 = status bits: bit0 mute, bit1 dim; on Monitor bits 3-5 = Monitor Out Trim index); [20] = oscillator byte; [25] = Monitor Out Trim index * 4; [26] = brightness 0-100. Payload 0x0c/0x18/0x6a/0x8e are documented above with their full-report equivalents. [17]/[19] also show a ~3 s connect blip like Orion (17: 0x08->0x00) -- but [19] is ALSO the clock source, so only the [17] change is pure noise. Offsets ~90/126/127 move on mixer-link writes or other mixer state; offset 122 is the confirmed 0x49 page selector (0f / 0c / 04 / 10). The 16 mixer-strip meter lanes at payload 0x8e..0x9d are dynamic and rest near 0x60 when idle; the 0xce/0xcf preamp lanes remain provisional mixed-signal candidates. [21-24] carry a sample-rate-derived clock word (moves with rate, like Orion @21-23).

meter_report.notes: The per-channel meter report -- magic 0x83 (Orion uses 0x75 for this; on the Zen Go 0x75 is instead the connect-time NAME/topology report). Resting values ~0x60 (96), drop toward 0 with signal, same inverted scale as Orion's meter. Header [4-5] = 0x0140. Byte-to-channel mapping not worked out.
meter_report.evidence: capture_09_idle_polling.pcapng: 0x83 frames 1:1 with 0x73; metering/ch1.pcapng..ch16.pcapng exercise one channel each (not yet diffed).

readback.status: CONFIRMED PRESENT 2026-09-01 -- the Zen Go speaks the SAME in-band readback protocol as the Orion Studio III (frame.readback there, PROTOCOL.md 4a), byte-for-byte identical request and response headers. Re-analysed from capture_01_enumeration.pcapng after the protocol was decoded on the Orion. This block replaces the old 'name_report' entry, which described the 0x75 frames as a Zen-Go-specific 'connect-time NAME/topology report' -- they are not: they are ordinary readback RESPONSES, and the ASCII was simply category 0x01 (device name + serial + firmware), the same category that carries it on the Orion.
readback.discriminator_note: On the Orion the discriminator matters because its METER report is also magic 0x75 (byte 1 = 0x1f). On the Zen Go the meter is magic 0x83 instead, so 0x75 is unambiguous here -- but the byte-1 check is kept so the same code path serves both devices.

categories.0x00: device id / firmware -- 2 bytes, observed `01 5a`. Orion's 0x00 is an ASCII firmware string ('4.41'); the Zen Go's is binary and NOT yet decoded (0x5a = 90; do not assume a version until confirmed).
categories.0x01: device name + serial + firmware revision -- 48 bytes, ASCII 'Zen Go Synergy C...' then the unit SERIAL then the fw rev. CONTAINS THE DEVICE SERIAL: never paste a raw dump of this category into the repo, an issue, or a capture that gets committed.
categories.0x03: routing / mixer-input assignment readback. This profile's capture-confirmed routing layouts cover indices 3, 4, 5, and 6-9 (3 = Record 1-8, 4 = SPDIF OUT, 5 = AFX IN, 6-9 = mixer inputs; 0-2 answer too but are not mapped here); body variants are documented in capture_dialect_variants below.
categories.0x04: mixer surface state. Indices 0 and 1 each return 16 two-byte strip records (fader level plus pan/mute/solo flags) in the capture dialect used by the profile. The device also answers indices 2 and 3 (the vendor panel reads all four on connect and its session dialog lists Mixer1..Mixer4), but the panel has pages for two only and nothing here writes the other two. Further in the same 133-byte record: body[66] = that mix's reverb return byte, and from body[69] the reverb send + send pan pairs of the 16 strips (meaningful in index 0).
categories.0x0a: Gazelle Reverb (AuraVerb) settings, index 0: see frame.auraverb_command.
categories.0x12: panning law, index 0: one byte, the params.pan_law index.
categories.0x16: mic emulation state, index 0: 4 bytes per preamp, read `00 00 00 32 | 00 00 00 32` all through the 2026-11-21 run (vendor session file names: target, emu_model, ch_swap, pattern = 0, 0, 0, 50). No write captured.
categories.0x17: reverb returns, index 0: body[0] = Monitor/HP1 return, body[1] = HP2 return, each level | 0x80 when muted (params.reverb_return). body[2..3] read 60 60 and were never written.
categories.0x0b: mixer-link selector state. The capture-confirmed index 3 response is a 24-byte bitmap: byte N is nonzero when wire selector N is linked; selectors 0-7 belong to Mix 1 and 16-23 to Mix 2.

categories.0x19: AFX strip order. The vendor panel queries indices 0-11 on connect (owner's unit fw 05.04, vendor panel 1.1.26 under Wine, usbmon capture panels_connect_walk.pcapng (sha256 a29c54490617ced77a07ba4f41e02d9aeafadd09c9827fbdbc1fb0b0ef90ce29), 2026-11-17: the panel's own connect walk). Each body is {type, inst} byte pairs, zero-padded; an empty rack returns an all-zero body. On the owner's unit index 0 returned `01 00 24 00 1b 00` (types 1, 36, 27, all instance 0) and indices 1-11 were empty; the same walk then issued tagged cat 0x07 queries for exactly types 1, 27 and 36 (index 0x80000000 | type), which ties the pair layout to this device. Index 0 is mixer channel 1 (vendor panel observation, see afx_inserts). No writes captured.

readback.observed_walk: The Zen Go Launcher's connect walk is TINY compared to the Orion's: only 3 queries, categories 0x00 / 0x01 / 0x11, each at index 0 (identical in capture_01_enumeration.pcapng and capture_01_enumeration_diff_filter.pcapng). The Orion walks 113 records across 10 categories. So this capture gives us NO record counts for any category.
readback.hazard: !! COMPLETE CATEGORY COUNTS ARE NOT KNOWN FOR THIS DEVICE. !! On the Orion, an out-of-range readback index crashes the firmware outright (Cortex-M BusFault, physical power cycle required -- see orion_studio_sc.json frame.readback.hazard). The Zen Go is the same protocol family and must be assumed to share the flaw. Its connect walk queries only index 0 of three categories, so `category_counts` remains EMPTY. The WebUI may use only the explicitly capture-confirmed feature layouts (routing cat 0x03 indices 3, 4, 5, 6-9; mixer cat 0x04 indices 0-1; link bitmap cat 0x0b index 3; reverb cat 0x0a / 0x17 / 0x18 index 0; pan law cat 0x12 index 0); all other indices remain blocked until bounded by device evidence.

identity.notes: Category 0x01 is a 48-byte record of NUL-terminated ASCII at fixed offsets: model name @0, SERIAL @20 (13 chars), hardware revision @36, then 4 binary bytes @44 (little-endian u32; both units seen decode to mid-2021, so plausibly a build/calibration timestamp -- a GUESS, not confirmed). input_routing.notes: The vendor panel shows one source row for both mixer pages and writes destinations 6, 7, 8, and 9 identically in lockstep; slots 0-15 are the 16 mixer strips and slots 16-31 are MUTE. The device stores the four records separately: on the owner's unit groups 7-9 held MUTE on strips 7/8 while group 6 held EMU MIC 1/2 until the panel's first source change rewrote all four alike. This project therefore reads each group, changes the one slot and writes each group back, never a copy of group 6. strict (2026-11-21): strips 1-4 are locked because their source box writes group 5 (AFX IN) and the panel always sends 00 00, 00 01, 03 02, 03 03 for them here; banks 0x03-0x05 (AFX OUT, the loopbacks) are never offered for a mixer strip.

mixer.readback: No fader/pan/mute/solo changes appear in the 0x73 STATE REPORT. The in-band 0x74/0x75 category 0x04 layout for Mix 1 and Mix 2 is capture-confirmed (16 two-byte fader + pan/flags slots per mix), and q0b/03 is a capture-confirmed 24-byte mixer-link selector bitmap. Live round-trip on this profile remains to be checked. Checked against the 2026-11-21 panel run: mix 0 strip 16 and mix 1 strips 15/16 read back at body[2*strip] / body[2*strip+1] (0x57 = mute + pan 0x17, 0x82 = solo + pan 0x02).
mixer.notes: 2 mixes ('Mix 1' / 'Mix 2'), 16 input strips each and no separate master strip: the vendor panel has two pages (MONITOR/HP1 = mix 0, HEADPHONES 2 = mix 1) and no master fader. The device answers cat 0x04 index 0..3 (four mixers; the panel's session dialog lists Mixer1..Mixer4, the last two with level 96 where the first two hold 90), but nothing in the panel writes mixes 2 and 3 and this profile does not either. Each strip = fader + pan + mute + solo; the Gazelle Reverb send of mix 0 is a separate frame (frame.reverb_send_command). While two strips are linked the panel sends every strip change twice (partner first); linking copies solo / mute / fader of the clicked strip to its partner and unlinking leaves the partner as it is. See frame.mix_command. What each strip's input is comes from the 'channel assignments' routing (frame.routing_command).

family_notes._comment: Antelope Synergy Core HID protocol family. Shared: magic 0x70 command / opcode @4 / param_id @16 / 320-byte reports / EP 0x01 OUT + 0x82 IN on HID interface 3. Param IDs are largely shared (0x50 gain, 0x4f mode, 0x51 phantom, 0x52 phase, 0x47/0x48 bus, 0x12/0x03 sample rate, 0x14/0xa2 link, 0x53/0xd3 routing). NOT shared / device-specific: report magics (Zen Go meter = 0x83, Orion = 0x75; Zen Go 0x75 = name report), the mixer opcode + shape (Zen Go 0x16/0xd4/subcmd 0x04, no send; Orion 0x17/0xd4/subcmd 0x05, has send), state-report offsets, channel/bus counts, source-bank numbers (Zen Go mute = 0x08, osc = 0x09, emumic = 0x0a; Orion mute = 0x0b, osc = 0x0c, emumic = 0x01).
siblings: profiles/orion_studio_sc.json (Orion Studio III, pid 0xa221) -- the reference, richest profile
carried_hazards: An unrecognised opcode cost a physical power cycle on the Discrete 8 Pro, and a 0x61 'unknown opcode' error frame exists in the family -- do NOT send frame.observed_opcodes or any opcode not in constraints.allowed_opcodes.
An out-of-range channel/bus index BusFaulted a Discrete 8 Pro -- validate targets before writing.
Discrete 8 Pro HID report descriptor has no Report ID, so Linux hidraw writes are 321 bytes (leading 0x00 + 320 payload). Check the Zen Go's descriptor before writing from Linux.
min write interval ~250 ms on Discrete 8 Pro (Orion tolerates ~30-80 ms); unknown for Zen Go -- rate-limit.

constraints.protected_mute_buses_note: On this device a dim write (on or off) clears the mute bit. No action other than an explicit mute write may un-mute an output: dim and mono are refused while a bus reads muted or unread (WebUI bus-toggle, CLI set-bus-dim / set-bus-mono), and the bus self-tests skip these buses. The owner's Monitor is normally muted.
constraints.gain_bounds_note: All Zen Go bounds are conservative/approximate because the captures did not always sweep to the rail; line -6..20 is the observed signed range, Hi-Z is approximately 0..45, and mic 0..65 comes from the A1/A2 mic-gain sweeps.
constraints.value_from_user_input: never send a raw value straight from user input; clamp to the documented range
